title: Regular-pullback transition comparison over base codimension at most one
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $r:P\to X$ be a regular morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes [def-exc-excellent-ring]; regular means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] with fibres that remain regular after every finite residue-field extension [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Assume $\ell$ is invertible. Let $\delta_X$ be a dimension function and $(K,(p_x))$ a pinned potential dualizing complex [def-per-potential-dualizing]. Define maps $p^r_t$ as follows. For $x=r(t)$ localize $X$ at $x$, write $i:P_x\hookrightarrow P\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for the closed fibre and $q:P_x\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$, and use [lem-per-regular-closed-support-base-change] to identify $i^!r^*K$ with $q^*R\Gamma_xK$. Apply $q^*p_x$, then on the regular fibre use the inverse absolute-purity class at $t$ [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus]. Thus
$$p^r_t:C_t(r^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(\delta_X(r(t))-b(t))[2\delta_X(r(t))-2b(t)],\qquad b(t)=\dim\mathcal O_{P_{r(t)},t}.$$
For every geometric specialization $t'\rightsquigarrow t$ over $x'\rightsquigarrow x$ such that $c_X(x',x)\leq1$, these maps identify the generalized transition of [lem-per-general-costalk-transitions] with the identity of the correspondingly twisted copy of $\Lambda$. Explicitly, with $c=c_P(t',t)$, the maps on cohomology satisfy
$$H^i(p^r_{t'})=H^{i+2c}(p^r_t(c))\circ\operatorname{sp}^{i}_{t',t}.$$
Targets are identified by $\delta_X(x')-b(t')=\delta_X(x)-b(t)+c$. No restriction is placed on $c_P(t',t)$, and the assertion is only for base codimension zero or one, not for arbitrary base specializations.

proof.text: Use exponent $n=1$ in the coefficient conventions of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. The canonical identification $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z=\mathbf F_\ell$ identifies its twists with those of [def-per-potential-dualizing]: both positive twists are powers of $\mu_\ell$ and both negative twists are dual powers. Both costalks are the same supported inverse images after localization. Both immediate transition maps take the reduced closure in the same strict localization, apply the same trait cochain model, and multiply by the inverse of the same residue degree after normalization. Thus the given pinned potential $K$ is also a pinned potential in the exponent-one conventions, with exactly the same maps, rather than merely an isomorphic unnormalized dualizing object.

Apply [lem-per-regular-pullback-pinnings] with $h=r$ and $n=1$. The hypotheses are precisely a regular morphism of Noetherian excellent schemes, invertibility of $\ell$, a dimension function, and a pinned potential $K$; no finite-type or compactifiability hypothesis is required. It gives the dimension function $\delta_r(t)=\delta_X(r(t))-b(t)$ and potential pinnings on $r^*K$, defined by the exchange of [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change], then $q^*p_x$, then the inverse class of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] at $n=1$. These are the maps $p^r_t$ of the item. First, the comparison $q^*R\Gamma_xK\to i^!r^*K$ of [lem-per-regular-closed-support-base-change] is characterized by its statement: after $i_*$, its composite with the supported counit is $r^*$ of the supported counit. The exchange of [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change] commutes with the closed counits by its statement. Since $i_*$ is left adjoint to $i^!$, a map into $i^!r^*K$ is determined by this composite, so the two comparisons are equal. Second, for the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{P_x,t}$ of regular affine Noetherian excellent schemes, [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus] states that its class is the absolute-purity Gysin class, and [lem-per-immersion-class-calculus] states that this class is the immersion class of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] (with $\mathbf Z/\ell=\mathbf F_\ell$). Thus the inverse classes agree. Hence the result applies to the item's specified maps, and their immediate-specialization squares commute in the derived category.

proof.text: For a positive-codimension geometric specialization $t\prime\rightsquigarrow t$, [lem-per-general-costalk-transitions] gives an immediate factorization $t_0=t\prime\rightsquigarrow t_1\rightsquigarrow\cdots\rightsquigarrow t_N=t$, and additivity of codimensions gives $N=c_P(t\prime,t)=c$. Since $\delta_r$ is a dimension function by Step 2, each edge gives $\delta_r(t_{j-1})=\delta_r(t_j)+1$ by [def-per-potential-dualizing]. Summing yields $\delta_r(t\prime)=\delta_r(t)+c$, which is the required target identification. For codimension zero the underlying point is unchanged and the same equality holds with $c=0$.

Take cohomology in the immediate compatibility squares from Step 2, using [def-per-potential-dualizing], and compose along the chain of Step 3. More explicitly, induction on $j$ starts with $j=0$ and the identity map, and the edge compatibility, twisted by $(j-1)$, replaces $H^{i+2(j-1)}(p^r_{t_{j-1}}(j-1))$ by $H^{i+2j}(p^r_{t_j}(j))$ composed with that edge transition. After $j$ edges one therefore has $H^i(p^r_{t_0})=H^{i+2j}(p^r_{t_j}(j))$ composed with the chain transition. At $j=c$, [lem-per-general-costalk-transitions] identifies this chain transition with $\operatorname{sp}^i_{t\prime,t}$, giving the claimed formula. If $c=0$, that node identifies the transition with geometric transport; the residue-field-site pinnings are morphisms of sheaves and hence commute with this transport. Finally restrict to the requested specializations with $c_X(x\prime,x)\leq1$. The chain used above need not remain over an immediate base specialization, since Step 2 already supplies potentiality on all of $P$.
